understanding: Cover IIR bit0 pending flag, bits3-1 priority codes for five sources, and fixed compatibility bits sampled on IIR reads.
preconditions: IIR accessible as 8-bit read-only at bus pin value wb_adr_i==2 via wishbone_slave_interface with normal registers selected
Single UART instance with clock edges available for sampling and reset released from C1h state
Owning traffic sequences capable of producing RLS RDA Timeout THRE and Modem pending states executed by their agents
Passive observation only with no driving of IIR or int_o
coverage_steps: WAIT for Wishbone read completion to address 2 observed via wishbone_slave_interface on clock edge
SAMPLE cp_iir_pending from bit0: IF bit0==0 THEN bin pending_0 ELSE IF bit0==1 THEN bin no_pending_1
SAMPLE cp_iir_code from bits 3-1: bins code_011_rls and code_010_rda and code_110_timeout and code_001_thre and code_000_modem; illegal codes 100_101_111 must never occur
SAMPLE cp_iir_fixed from bits 7-6 and 5-4: IF bits7-6==11 THEN bin fixed_76_11; IF bits5-4==00 THEN bin fixed_54_00; any other fixed bits illegal
FOR each IIR read REPEAT sampling until all legal pending and code and fixed bins are hit
completion: End collection after owning traffic sequences complete plus drain_cycles to flush pending IIR read events
Abort on request_timeout_cycles operational limit; timeout is testbench limit not DUT timing

facts.statement: IIR bit0 0 means interrupt pending, 1 means no interrupt pending.
facts.quote:
Bit 0 indicates that an interrupt is pending when it’s logic ‘0’. When it’s ‘1’ – no interrupt
is pending.

facts.statement: IIR reports current highest priority pending interrupt.
facts.quote:
The IIR enables the programmer to retrieve what is the current highest priority pending
interrupt.

facts.statement: IIR 011 is 1st priority Receiver Line Status from parity overrun framing break cleared by reading LSR.
